messages:
Maria L: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the FP8 mixed-precision matmul after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak. Repro at scale when KV cache is reused. ~8% slower p50 and a small 1e-3 drift on our float checksum tests.
Kevin H: Reproable locally? which branch/commit and test command?
Maria L: repro on `main` @ commit 7a3d2f1 (batching heuristic change). Test run command:
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/perf/test_matmul_mixedprec.py::test_fp8_kv_reuse -q --runslow
```
Samir P: I saw this too. kernel selection flips from `fp8_gemm_v2` -> `bf16_fallback_gemm` once batch_size >= 8 because the heuristic picks the lower-latency kernel for cold cache. That switch looks correlated with the slowdown.
Tess O: We got an alert on the bench cluster when the change landed. Pushed a trace. @bench-bot can you paste the flame/percentile summary?
bench-bot: quick profile snippet from bench-staging: 
```
%time per token: 12.4ms -> 13.4ms (p50)
kernel timeline: fp8_gemm_v2 (0-120s) -> bf16_fallback_gemm (120-240s)
KV reuse hit rate: 86%
```
Maria L: Key detail: when kernel flips mid-session we see an extra memcpy in the KV hot-path. Suspect pack layout differs between fp8_gemm_v2 and bf16_fallback_gemm so we do a copy/convert on reuse. That kills throughput.
Jing W: I can reproduce with a short script that pulses batch size. Looks like calibration runs (per-batch quant param recompute) also kick in on the fallback, introducing both latency and small numeric drift. I'll open a minimal repro.
Kevin H: Short-term mitigation: pin kernel selection per-session once KV_hits > X. If a kernel switch is required, invalidate KV entirely rather than attempt a conversion in hot-path. Proposed patch:
```python
if kv_hits > STABLE_THRESHOLD:
    selected_kernel = session.bound_kernel
else:
    selected_kernel = heuristic_pick()
```
Tess O: Agree with pinning. Also disabling per-batch calibrate when KV present reduced the numeric drift in our canary. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout blocked until a patch lands. Jira INF-3421 created.
Samir P: I'll add instrumentation for pack/unpack offsets and assert checks in CI to detect layout mismatches early. If it's a layout mismatch, fixes are straightforward.
Maria L: Thanks — I'll attach the bench logs and the minimal repro to INF-3421. Can we aim for a patch + staging verify by EOD?
Kevin H: I'll draft the kernel-pin patch and run overnight staging runs. cc @Tess O for oncall verification tomorrow morning.
Tess O: I'll keep an eye on staging runs. If we see any remaining drift I'll flip per-batch-calibration off for canary.
Maria L: Great. Thanks everyone.
